subject: POC trial planning - workload & success criteria (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: POC trial planning - workload & success criteria (Acme Health)

Hi Alex -

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a proposed plan for the POC/trial so we can align on success criteria, timelines, and owners. Please review and flag anything missing.

High-level success criteria (proposal)
- Functional: Redwood serving should meet Acme's core flows with >=95% of calls returning production-grade outputs (no major hallucination/regression) compared to your baseline.
- Performance: p95 latency for single-request flows < 300ms (under target RPS, see below).
- Reliability: error rate < 0.5% for the duration of the trial.
- Cost/throughput: demonstrate predictable unit cost within your target budget for targeted workload.

Workload & traffic profile (please confirm below)
- Steady RPS: 25-35 RPS (avg) during business hours.
- Peak bursts: up to ~200 RPS for 2-5 minute windows (morning batch/standups).
- Token profile: prompt avg ~100 tokens, completion avg ~60 tokens; max observed up to 512 tokens.
- Concurrency: typical active concurrency 6-10, sustained concurrency target for trial 8.
- Patterns: predictable morning spike (08:30-09:30 local), lighter afternoons, occasional evening async burst.

Evaluation plan (2-week trial recommended)
- Week 0: onboarding & sandbox creds, import sample dataset, configure routes. (Owner: Marissa)
- Week 1: synthetic load tests + replay of sampled traffic (Owner: Dylan).
- Week 2: run live shadowing/feature-flagged traffic with progressive ramp; collect latency/cost/quality metrics (Owners: Alex product team + Monica for CS).

Ownership
- Trial owner (Acme): Alex Chen (product) and Jordan Lee (platform).
- Redwood POC lead: Marissa Cole (AE).
- Infra/test harness: Dylan Brooks (Solutions).
- Success/quality tracking: Monica Patel (Customer Success).

Next steps
1) Please confirm the workload numbers above (RPS, token lengths, concurrency) and any other constraints (data residency, IP allowlists).
2) If agreed, we'll provision a trial environment and send credentials + an intake spreadsheet to collect sample payloads (attached).
3) Proposed tentative kickoff: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 - 09:00 PT. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite.

Attachments: acme-workload-intake.xlsx (blank intake for sample payloads and test accounts)

Thanks - looking forward to running this with you.


Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192


From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial planning - workload & success criteria (Acme Health)

Thanks Marissa - this lines up well with our notes. A few confirmations and clarifications from our side: 

Workload details (confirmed)
- Steady RPS: we currently see ~30 RPS on average for the feature we want to test.
- Peak bursts: we can see spikes up to 180-200 RPS for 3-5 minutes, usually 08:15-08:45 local.
- Token lengths: prompts avg ~90 tokens; completions avg ~60 tokens; we do have longer med/long background prompts that can reach 400-512 tokens for some clinical summarization flows.
- Concurrency: typically 6-10 concurrent callers; during internal load tests we've hit sustained 12 for short periods.

Constraints
- Data residency: all data must remain in the us-east region for the trial.
- IP allowlist: we will provide 2 static egress IPs for initial testing.

Timeline
- 2-week trial is fine. Prefer kickoff 2 Jun and start synthetic runs same week.

Attachments: I'll send our SOC2 excerpt and a short network diagram to Jordan and Marissa after this (SOC2 reference).

On the success criteria, the p95 < 300ms looks reasonable but if you can show p99 < 750ms on our 2-week traffic that would be a strong signal for us.

Thanks - Alex
Alex Chen
Product Manager, Acme Health
alex.chen@acmehealth.com | +1 (617) 555-3321

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial planning - workload & success criteria (Acme Health)

Alex/Marissa - quick note on environment and next steps from the sales/ops side.

- We can provision a US-only trial sandbox scoped to the workload above. For the proposed traffic (30 RPS steady, 200 RPS short bursts) we'll allocate a dedicated pool sized to target p95 < 300ms for your average payload sizes. Dylan will validate during the synthetic run.
- Pricing: for trial purposes we'll provide a capped evaluation credit covering the two-week run. If we need to extend or increase capacity, I'll follow up with a contract addendum. Deal id RDW-2026-ACME-47.
- DocuSign: I've created the trial SOW and sent it to your legal inbox - link below. If you can get that back by end of week we can lock the 2 Jun kickoff.

Related links: https://www.docusign.com/DocuSign/Envelope/RDW-2026-ACME-47

Perfect - thanks everyone for the confirmations. Quick updated plan and checklist before kickoff on Tue, 2 Jun: 

Pre-kickoff (this week)
- Jordan: send IP allowlist + network diagram (action: Jordan) - due Fri, 29 May.
- Acme legal: sign the trial SOW in DocuSign (action: Acme legal / Jordan).
- Acme: populate acme-workload-intake.xlsx with 3 representative sample payloads and credential/test account info (action: Alex).
- Redwood: provision US sandbox + create test harness repo access (action: Dylan).

Kickoff (Tue, 2 Jun - 09:00 PT)
- Attendees: Alex, Jordan, Marissa, Ben, Dylan, Monica. Agenda: environment walkthrough, intake review, test plan and ramp schedule, observability/metric hooks.

During trial (weeks 1-2)
- Run synthetic replay + live shadowing. Dylan will share load scripts and coordinates for running your internal tests. Monica will collect quality/regression notes and track success metrics.
- Weekly sync: Fri 11:00 PT (first check-in Fri, 5 Jun).

Deliverables/outcomes
- Consolidated metrics dashboard (latency percentiles, error rate, tokens/cost) - Redwood provides link.
- Post-trial readout with go/no-go recommendation and estimated unit cost from Redwood (owner: Ben).

Attachments: acme-workload-intake.xlsx (filled template expected from Acme), SOC2-Q4-2025.pdf (Redwood SOC2 excerpt)

If that all looks good I'll send the calendar invites and add the test-harness link to the shared Drive folder.

Thanks - and excited to get started.


Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
